concerns.text: The baseline neural‑teacher is trained on the original Causal Forcing++ dataset while the physics‑teacher student is trained on synthetic Box2D data. This introduces a confound between teacher type and data distribution, making it impossible to attribute performance differences solely to the teacher signal.
No explicit power analysis is provided for the paired t‑test. The plan assumes ≥0.8 power for a medium effect size without justification, risking inconclusive statistical results.

The chosen metrics (SSIM, PSNR, LPIPS, FID) assess visual fidelity and generative richness but do not directly measure the quality of the *teacher* signal (i.e., how well the physics trajectory captures causal structure). Relying on these metrics may lead to construct validity issues for the core hypothesis.

Success Criterion SC-005 (computational feasibility: ≤ 6 h wall‑clock, ≤ 7 GB RAM) is absent from the task mapping. No task claims to verify or enforce the runtime and memory limits required by the spec.

concerns.location: plan.md:Performance Goals section (line ~45) & Compute Feasibility Summary (line ~120)
concerns.text: The plan asserts a full CPU‑only pipeline ≤ 6 h wall‑clock with a 50 M‑parameter diffusion student model trained for ≤ 20 epochs on ~10 k sequences. Empirically, training a diffusion model of this size on CPU (even with batch‑size 8) typically exceeds 12 h on a GitHub Actions free runner, making the stated compute budget unrealistic. This violates the methodology requirement that the approach be runnable within the free‑compute constraints.

The data model lists three primary entities (PhysicsTrajectory, VideoSequence, EvaluationResults) but only provides schemas for PhysicsTrajectory and EvaluationResults. No schema/contract is defined for VideoSequence, yet the plan (e.g., T1.2) creates and uses VideoSequence objects. Add a `video_sequence.schema.yaml` contract and reference it in the plan to keep the data model and contracts consistent.

The plan validates the physics‑teacher model by computing SSIM, PSNR, and LPIPS against the *same* physics‑generated videos that serve as the model’s output (see T4.1–T4.3). Because the ground‑truth for the physics teacher is definitionally identical to its predictions, these metrics are guaranteed to be perfect (SSIM = 1, PSNR = ∞, LPIPS = 0). The subsequent paired t‑test (T5.1) therefore compares a constant‑value distribution to the neural‑teacher’s scores, violating the independence assumption of the test and rendering the statistical conclusion circular and non‑informative.

new_concerns.location: plan.md:Section 4 – Evaluation & Metric Computation / Section 5 – Statistical Analysis
new_concerns.text: The primary statistical comparison (paired t‑test) pits the physics‑teacher model against the neural‑teacher baseline trained on the original Causal Forcing++ dataset, while both are evaluated on a test set derived from synthetic physics data. This leaves a data‑distribution confound: performance differences may stem from mismatched training data rather than the teacher signal itself. Although a control neural‑teacher trained on the synthetic data is added (Task 2.4), it is not incorporated into the main paired analysis, so the core hypothesis remains inadequately isolated.

Success Criterion SC-008 (Summarise regression results (Pearson r, p‑value) in a table) is not referenced by any task. The current ablation tasks (T6.2, T6.3) cite SC‑006 but omit SC‑008, leaving the spec unaddressed.

new_concerns.text: The model_type enum lists only "physics_teacher" and "neural_teacher", but the plan now evaluates three models (student, control baseline on physics data, original-data baseline). Per-sequence metrics for the student and control models cannot be recorded under this schema, breaking the paired t-test data flow (T5.1). Extend the enum (e.g., add "student", "neural_teacher_physics").

The new schema's frame_rate description is corrupted/truncated: "fixed to a consistent **t**?  # Note: retained original wording". This is not a valid schema description; restore a complete sentence (e.g., "fixed to a consistent frame rate for all sequences").

Plan and research.md state the student model is ~10 M parameters, but spec FR-002 and the Compute-feasibility assumption specify ≈ 50 M parameters. Cross-doc disagreement; align the plan with the spec or record a justified deviation.

The model_type enum only allows "physics_teacher" and "neural_teacher", but the plan (T4.1–T4.4, quickstart step 7) evaluates a student model and a control baseline on the same test set; per-sequence EvaluationResults for those models cannot validate against this contract. Extend the enum (e.g., "student", "neural_teacher_physics") or document how student/control predictions are recorded.

The new Trajectory‑Pixel Correlation metric (Pearson r between physics velocities and optical‑flow vectors of the rendered frames) is tautological: the frames are rendered deterministically FROM the physics positions/velocities (T1.1–T1.2), so pixel motion is by construction a projection of the trajectory. The correlation can only "confirm" signal fidelity; it cannot return an informative negative result. To be non‑circular it must be computed on STUDENT-generated frames (does the student reproduce the teacher-driven motion?), not on the ground-truth rendered frames.

The enum still lists only "physics_teacher" and "neural_teacher" as generating models, but the revised design evaluates student and control-baseline predictions against ground-truth frames. The enum should reflect the models actually scored (student, neural_teacher, control) to avoid re-introducing the retired "physics_teacher as predictor" framing at implementation time.
